summary: The main article describes an NHC/photoredox dual catalytic system for the Suzuki-type cross-coupling of alkyl trifluoroborates with acid fluorides. It includes optimization tables, substrate scope tables for ketones and alpha-silyl carbazoles, and detailed mechanistic schemes including control experiments and Stern-Volmer plots.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Research motivation for NHC/photoredox dual catalysed Suzuki-type coupling reactions.
items.description: This scheme outlines the challenges of classical Suzuki-Miyaura cross-coupling and the proposed NHC/photoredox dual catalysis approach for activating alkyl boron reagents.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimisation of reaction conditions
items.description: This table details the screening of photocatalysts, NHC catalysts, solvents, and bases to optimize the yield of ketone 3a.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Substrate scope of the cross-coupling of acid fl uorides and alkyl tri fl uoroborates
items.description: This table demonstrates the reaction's compatibility with various substituted alkyl trifluoroborates and aroyl fluorides, including late-stage functionalization examples.

items.heading: Table 3
items.caption: Cross-coupling of acyl fl uorides and a -silyl carbazole 4
items.description: This table explores the expandability of the protocol to the acylation of alpha-silyl carbazoles with various acyl fluorides.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Control experiments and the light on -o ff experiment.
items.description: This scheme presents mechanistic control experiments, including TEMPO quenching and light on/off cycles to confirm the radical nature of the reaction.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Mechanistic investigations of the reaction.
items.description: This scheme includes UV-vis absorption spectra, Stern-Volmer quenching plots, and cyclic voltammograms used to study the energy transfer process.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Plausible reaction pathway.
items.description: A proposed catalytic cycle involving energy transfer from the excited photocatalyst to the acyl azolium intermediate followed by radical coupling.
